Subject: ACME discovery — integration & model routing follow-up

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so we have alignment: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use case: ACME wants live summary + reranking for internal support KB, with a fallback to smaller, cheaper models for high-throughput endpoints.
- Expected throughput: ~20 reqs/sec at peak, typical context ~1k tokens.
- Latency SLO: sub-250ms for user-facing summaries; batch jobs can be higher.

Integration/architecture points we discussed (high level):
- SDK & auth: We support API key auth for server-side calls; for client-side, we recommend proxying through a short-lived token or your backend. Sample SDKs are available for Node/Python/Go.
- Model routing: You can route by policy (latency-first, cost-first, region) and define fallback chains (e.g., rtx-large -> rtx-medium -> rtx-small).
- Structured output & tool calling: Our runtime supports function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs via a schema validation layer. Good for extracting entities and action items.
- Embeddings & reranker: We recommend embedding-heavy semantic search for candidate retrieval and a lightweight reranker (embed + small model) to keep cost down.

Attachments: integration_diagram.png (high-level flow).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with your infra/eng (30–45m) — can we schedule for Wed/Thu this week? 
2) Share SDK quickstart and an example policy config for model routing — Marcus and Dev will put together config suggestions.
3) Pilot: 2-week pilot with a dedicated test endpoint (we can size a small Dedicated pool if needed).

Would Thursday 3/12 at 10am PT work for a technical call? If that doesn't work, tell me a few slots and we’ll coordinate.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Alice — confirmed for Thu 3/12 10am PT (calendar invite sent). Marcus/Dev — attaching a simple integration diagram and linking an SDK quickstart. Marcus will bring a sample policy to the call.

Quick answers:
- Short-lived tokens / OIDC: Yes — Redwood supports OIDC token exchange (your IdP) for provisioning short-lived inference tokens. We also support KMS-wrapped API keys for server-side. We'll include the OIDC flow doc in the drive folder.
- Fallback example (high-level):
  1) Route request by policy: if region==us-west and latency_slo_ms<=250 -> route to rtx-low-latency-16k (primary).
  2) If primary unavailable or error/timeout >150ms -> failover to rtx-cost-8k (fallback-1) which is quantized for lower cost, slightly lower throughput.
  3) If fallback-1 saturated -> route to rtx-micro as last resort (lowest cost, degraded quality).

I'll also include a concrete sample JSON policy in the Drive folder before the call (simple routing rules + per-model per-route cost cap).

Subject: Internal: ACME technical notes / ask before Thu call

Quick internal notes for the call with ACME (Thu 3/12 10am PT). Please keep these points ready and add any specifics you want to present: 

1) Auth & SDK
- Bring a 3–5 line Node snippet showing OIDC token exchange -> short-lived inference token, plus server-side API key flow. Keep it ops-friendly.

2) Model routing policy (recommendation)
- Goal: meet 250ms P95 for user-facing summary with cost target <= $0.02/interaction.
- Proposed policy (example bullet):
  - Primary: rtx-low-latency-16k (route when region==us-west AND expected_tokens<=1200 AND latency_budget_ms<=250).
  - Fallback-1 (on timeout/error/saturation): rtx-cost-8k (quantized, lower cost).
  - Fallback-2 (if still failing): rtx-micro (degraded quality).
- Include per-route rate limits and a circuit-breaker: if fallback error rate >5% in 5m window, alert + open circuit to prevent cascading errors.

3) Embeddings + reranker flow
- Retrieval: user query -> FAISS on embeddings (embed_model_v2).
- Rerank: top-10 candidates -> reranker model (small cross-encoder or embed-score + lightweight scorer).
- Cost control: do candidate narrowing (embedding similarity threshold) before calling reranker; batch reranker calls where possible.

4) Structured output & tool calling
- Confirm we can provide schema validation on structured output (we do). Prepare examples for extracting: ticket_id, urgency, suggested_articles.
- Tool calling: show an example of invoking internal actions (open ticket) with an allowlist and signed webhook verification.

5) Region routing & data locality
- ACME requested US-only routing. Prepare a config snippet to pin routes to us-west/us-east and a fallback to multi-region only if explicitly allowed.

6) Pilot proposal logistics
- Size: start with 1-2 dedicated GPUs for pilot (small Dedicated pool). Offer 2-week pilot with telemetry dashboard and cost/latency report.

Attachables: integration_diagram.png (send link in the call).

Can you both add any model names, quantization notes, or sample policy JSON as replies here so I can drop into the Drive folder before the call?

Thanks — Marissa
